summary: Trending in the right direction after the psoas/groin injury that limited him through camp — head coach Sean McVay said Sept. 6 he's "making good progress" and is expected to play the Week 1 opener against San Francisco (in Melbourne, Australia).

Still faces potential discipline under the NFL's personal conduct policy after being sued for assault and battery (allegations include an anti-Jewish slur and biting) by a woman earlier in the offseason. The league has not ruled or placed him on the Commissioner Exempt List as of Sept. 6, so no games are expected to be missed yet, but the exposure is real and unresolved into Week 1.

Continuing to progress in his recovery from the torn ACL that ended his 2025 season at 4 games; said he feels "real good" and has been full-go in camp drills, but remained noncommittal on the record about Week 1 vs. Dallas, saying he won't force it if his knee isn't ready. Beat reporting characterizes him as trending toward playing barring a setback.

Placed on injured reserve (calf, designated to return) as part of San Francisco's initial 53-man roster; will miss at least the first four games. Comes on top of Ricky Pearsall's season-ending PCL surgery, leaving the 49ers' receiver room thinner than expected entering the season — re-signed Deebo Samuel and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling both get expanded early-season opportunity as a result.

Formally placed on injured reserve (designated to return) with the hamstring injury suffered in an Aug. 13 joint practice; the move guarantees the Saints' first-round rookie will miss at least the first four games and puts his return in the mid-October range around New Orleans' Week 8 bye.

Cleared the undisclosed injury that had sidelined him through much of camp — returned to practice in late August and is now expected to be ready for the Sept. 13 opener at Atlanta, per an updated team report.
Back at practice alongside DK Metcalf after each missed time in camp; both Steelers receivers are now expected to be full go for the Week 1 opener against Atlanta.

Has been sidelined by an undisclosed injury since Aug. 15 and did not practice as of Sept. 4, but CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reports "there's currently optimism" he'll be available for Buffalo's Sept. 13 opener against Houston; Buffalo's official Week 1 injury report was still pending as of this report.

Toe injury (suffered mid-August vs. the Jets) is still lingering enough that he sat out Tampa Bay's preseason finale to focus on recovery; as of Aug. 28 it's "not yet known" when he'll return to practice, leaving his Week 1 availability (Sept. 13 at Cincinnati) genuinely uncertain for the Bucs' clear No. 2 target behind Mike Evans' departure.

Sat out practice with a left knee hyperextension (bad landing on a deep-ball attempt) but downplayed it himself ("if I had a game tomorrow, I'd play"); coach Zac Taylor confirmed as of Sept. 1 that Chase will be limited in practice this week but is expected ready for the Sept. 13 opener vs. Tampa Bay.

Dealing with a heel contusion that limited him from practice; coach Zac Taylor said Sept. 1 it's minor ("Tee has a little heel contusion that'll limit him this week, but he and Ja'Marr will be good at the end of the week") and he's expected to be ready for the Sept. 13 opener at Tampa Bay.

Missed the preseason finale and a couple of camp practices with what he called a "very minor," precautionary calf issue; returned to practice Sept. 1-2 and looks on track for Indianapolis' Sept. 13 opener against Baltimore.

Signed with the Colts (1-year deal, up to $8.32M) as a complementary route-runner behind Alec Pierce and alongside Josh Downs, filling the WR3 void left by Michael Pittman's trade to Pittsburgh. GM Chris Ballard confirmed Sept. 1 that Allen will play in the Sept. 13 opener vs. Baltimore. Update to earlier reporting that had him unsigned as of late August.

Confirmed Sept. 2 that Patrick Mahomes (recovering from a torn ACL/LCL suffered in Week 15 of 2025, surgery Dec. 16) will start Week 1 against Denver — "Oh, he's back, ain't no potentially" — after the two worked together through offseason rehab to rebuild chemistry. Worthy is himself fully recovered from his own shoulder injury. A full-strength Mahomes (vs. the alternative of backup Justin Fields) is a real swing factor for the whole Chiefs receiving corps' Week 1 outlook.

The NFL concluded in late offseason review that Rice will not face personal-conduct discipline in 2026, clearing him to play a full season after a six-game suspension cost him the start of 2025. His outlook is now tied primarily to Patrick Mahomes' Week 1 QB status (Mahomes trending to start, per Xavier Worthy's Sept. 2 confirmation) rather than any of his own off-field exposure.

The two-way Heisman winner's offensive role has narrowed sharply heading into Week 1 — recent practices have him running almost exclusively at cornerback (20 of his last 20 snaps in one session), and he's set to start at CB opposite Montaric Brown in the opener vs. Cleveland. The Jaguars say they haven't abandoned using him at WR, but beat reporting frames his Sept. 13 offensive workload as a "handful of snaps" at most, well below the true two-way vision from the offseason.

Listed first at WR on Jacksonville's depth chart and drawing tight coverage from Travis Hunter (mostly playing CB now) in practice, but his target competition with Jakobi Meyers and a hot-camp Parker Washington remains live; after a sophomore slump (48/91 for 707 yards, 8.2 PPG in 2025), analysts still peg him as a riskier bet than his WR1 billing suggests.

Clean bill of health since late July and a full camp building chemistry with Jacoby Brissett; flashed in the preseason finale vs. the Raiders (a TD catch plus a drawn 20-yard pass interference). Listed as a Week 1 starter alongside Michael Wilson under new OC Mike LaFleur, reversing the earlier-camp narrative that had Wilson outproducing him.

Cleared his hamstring injury (off the injury report as of late August) and is now positioned as Philadelphia's clear lead receiver following the A.J. Brown trade to New England — the primary target in Jalen Hurts' passing attack entering the Sept. 13 opener vs. Washington.

Not appearing on New England's Week 1 injury report ahead of the Sept. 9 opener at Seattle, after dislocating (and popping back into place) his left thumb during an August practice and later avoiding a further non-contact injury scare on a slick practice field. No lingering concern in his first season as a Patriot after being traded from Philadelphia.

Re-signed by San Francisco after a 2025 season in Washington; now gets an expanded early-season role after Ricky Pearsall's season-ending PCL surgery and Christian Kirk's Aug. 30 IR placement (calf), pairing with Mike Evans and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling to open the season.

Rookie's real path to snaps got wider after Christian Kirk's Aug. 30 IR placement (calf) left San Francisco's receiver room down to Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans as the clear top two — Stribling now projects for early meaningful offensive work as a rookie with no prior-season stat line.

With his toe injury lingering into September, Tampa Bay's post-Mike-Evans passing-game distribution for Week 1 is genuinely uncertain — Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan stand to absorb extra early-season target share if Egbuka isn't full-go for the Sept. 13 opener at Cincinnati.

Returned to practice after a brief lower-body absence; Baltimore's captains/injury update through Sept. 3 frames the team as approaching Week 1 (Sept. 13 vs. Indianapolis) in good health, with no real threat to his availability as Lamar Jackson's top target.

Confirmed atop Denver's unofficial depth chart again for 2026 despite the offseason trade for Jaylen Waddle; expected to see reduced target volume as a result but retains his role as the offense's top red-zone threat and is on pace for a third straight 1,000-yard season.
